title: Electrodynamics: Motors, Generators and AC
seo_title: Grade 12 Physical Sciences: Electrodynamics: Motors, Generators and AC Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: Electric motors and generators: the motor effect and Fleming's left-hand rule; DC and AC generators and Faraday's law; alternating current: root mean square values, Vrms = Vmax/√2 and Pave = VrmsIrms; uses of AC and DC. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 12, Physics: Electrodynamics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): electric motors, generators, alternating current, rms values and average power. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A motor turns electrical energy into mechanical energy; a generator does the opposite.
body_html:
How to think about it

An electric motor works because a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a force (the motor effect); a split-ring commutator reverses the current every half turn so the coil keeps turning. A generator uses electromagnetic induction: a coil turning in a magnetic field has a changing flux, which induces an emf.

An AC generator uses slip rings and produces alternating current; a DC generator uses a split-ring commutator. Eskom supplies AC at 230 V (rms) and 50 Hz. The rms value is the DC value that would give the same power: Vrms = Vmax/√2, Irms = Imax/√2, and Pave = VrmsIrms.

Example

Vmax = 325 V. Vrms?

÷ √2

Answer: 230 V

Example

Which part of a DC motor reverses the current?

Two half rings

Answer: the split-ring commutator

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up slip rings and split rings.
  • Using peak values to find average power.
  • Thinking a generator makes energy from nothing.

faq.q: Why is electricity transmitted at very high voltage?
faq.a: For the same power the current is smaller, so less energy is lost as heat in the cables (P = I²R).

faq.q: Why is AC used for the grid?
faq.a: Its voltage can easily be stepped up and down with transformers.

items.q: What is the direction of the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field?
c: at right angles to both the current and the field (right-hand rule)
items.e: The force is greatest when the wire is at 90° to the field.

items.q: An ideal transformer has 50 turns on the primary and 1 000 on the secondary. The primary voltage is 400 V. Calculate the secondary voltage.
How does an AC generator produce a current?
c: a coil rotates in a magnetic field, so the flux through it changes and an e.m.f. is induced
items.e: Slip rings connect the coil to the circuit.

sets.title: Magnetic fields and the motor principle

items.q: Is steel a magnetic material?
items.e: Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic. Most other metals are not.

items.q: A wire carries a current into the page in a magnetic field that points to the right. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the force on the wire?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field (to the right), seCond finger = Current (into the page), thuMb = Motion/force (down the page).

items.q: You look at one end of a solenoid. The current flows clockwise around this end. What pole is this end?
c: no pole: the field is only inside
items.e: Clockwise current seen from an end makes it a south pole; anticlockwise makes it a north pole.

items.q: A wire carries a current into the page in a magnetic field that points down the page. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the force on the wire?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field (down the page), seCond finger = Current (into the page), thuMb = Motion/force (to the left).

items.q: A force of 1,25 N acts on a wire 0,25 m long in a magnetic field of 0,5 T (at right angles). What is the current? (F = BIl)
A wire carries a current to the left in a magnetic field that points into the page. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the force on the wire?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field (into the page), seCond finger = Current (to the left), thuMb = Motion/force (down the page).

items.q: A force of 0,5 N acts on a wire 0,25 m long in a magnetic field of 0,25 T (at right angles). What is the current? (F = BIl)
A north pole is brought near a north pole. Why do they repel?
items.e: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

items.q: The north pole of one magnet is brought near the north pole of another. What happens?
items.e: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

items.q: A wire 0,25 m long carries a current of 4 A at right angles to a magnetic field of 0,4 T. What is the force on the wire? (F = BIl)
A wire carries a current down the page in a magnetic field that points to the left. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the force on the wire?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field (to the left), seCond finger = Current (down the page), thuMb = Motion/force (into the page).

items.q: Is nickel a magnetic material?
items.e: Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic. Most other metals are not.

items.q: A long straight wire carries a current into the page. Seen from the front, what is the direction of the magnetic field lines around the wire?
c: straight lines away from the wire
items.e: Right-hand grip rule: thumb along the current, curled fingers give the field direction (out of the page: anticlockwise).

items.q: A wire carries a current into the page in a magnetic field that points up the page. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the force on the wire?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field (up the page), seCond finger = Current (into the page), thuMb = Motion/force (to the right).

items.q: The south pole of one magnet is brought near the south pole of another. What happens?
items.e: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

items.q: A wire in a magnetic field pointing to the left feels a force out of the page. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the current?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field, seCond finger = Current, thuMb = force. The current flows up the page.

items.q: A long straight wire carries a current out of the page. Seen from the front, what is the direction of the magnetic field lines around the wire?
c: straight lines away from the wire
items.e: Right-hand grip rule: thumb along the current, curled fingers give the field direction (out of the page: anticlockwise).

items.q: A north pole is brought near a south pole. Why do they attract?
items.e: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

items.q: A wire in a magnetic field pointing down the page feels a force into the page. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the current?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field, seCond finger = Current, thuMb = force. The current flows to the right.
